principles: Harden general Koala mechanisms, never PVSC-specific runtime cases.
Prefer shared oracle functions and receipts over duplicated status wording.
Keep safety gates stricter than status hints and make failures observable.
Treat tests as regression contracts for process risks, not as proof by narrative.
drivers: False-green validation is the highest blast-radius failure.
CLI users and agents need exact field-level failures to recover quickly.
DONE guidance must be based on the same blockers the gate will enforce.
Koala-generated metadata must be safe to reconcile without deleting human drafts.

options.name: A: Conservative hardening and regression coverage
pros: Strengthens already-present mechanisms without rewriting lifecycle flow
Lowest risk for current users and active stories
cons: Leaves some project-specific test quality concerns as advisory rather than hard gate
Requires careful tests to prove existing behavior rather than visible large refactor

options.name: B: Rewrite validate/status/DONE flow around a new unified engine
pros: Could produce a cleaner long-term architecture
Could make every renderer consume one new API immediately
cons: High regression risk in lifecycle code
Likely overkill because many shared row contracts already exist
Would slow delivery and create migration burden

options.name: C: Add PVSC-specific guards and exact pytest thresholds
pros: Directly prevents the recently observed PVSC symptom
cons: Would break or confuse non-Python projects
Would encode stale story-specific facts into runtime behavior

chosen: A: Conservative hardening and regression coverage
rationale: Choose conservative hardening because the codebase already contains the correct shape for validate receipts, schema errors, DONE pre-check rows, and stray artifact cleanup. The story should close gaps and add user-visible advisory coverage without destabilizing the lifecycle.

preMortem.scenario: Validation hardening accidentally makes valid configured commands fail on Windows or simple npm test projects.
preMortem.trigger: Treating every string command as shell-only or changing argv splitting too broadly.
preMortem.consequence: Existing projects lose validation capability or see confusing command errors.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep current string parsing rules, add focused smoke tests for shell and non-shell command receipts, and preserve structured command entries with explicit args.

preMortem.scenario: Status/next wording still diverges from DONE gate after the patch.
preMortem.trigger: Adding another renderer-specific string instead of relying on DONE pre-check rows.
preMortem.consequence: Agents again attempt story_advance DONE before summary, delivery-check, or dirty-tree blockers are resolved.
preMortem.mitigation: Test session_brief and next together against synthetic TEST story blockers and assert no optimistic DONE shortcut appears.

preMortem.scenario: Whitelist cleanup deletes a human draft file because the whitelist is too broad.
preMortem.trigger: Matching directories or prefixes instead of precise generated filenames.
preMortem.consequence: User loses untracked notes during DONE merge cleanup.
preMortem.mitigation: Whitelist only exact basename entries for known Koala artifacts and keep non-whitelisted files blocking with stash/rm instructions.

preMortem.scenario: Doctor/advisory becomes a hard gate and blocks healthy projects without pytest or validate.ts.
preMortem.trigger: Promoting fallback warnings into validation failure globally.
preMortem.consequence: Koala becomes hostile for small or nonstandard projects.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep doctor validation-risk checks advisory, while required validate command execution remains hard fail only when a configured/required command exists and fails.
